title: Generative AI consulting: what should you walk away with?
description: Generative AI consulting for firms of 40 to 500 staff: what to get, which plans keep prompts private, and how to test advisors.
verdict: Good help leaves you with two or three measured tasks, not a roadmap deck.[^1][^6]
Your staff already use AI. Give them a business-tier plan that does not train on their prompts.[^8][^38]
Expect help for your people, not cuts. Most AI-using firms use it to assist staff, not take over tasks.[^1][^18]
Test any advisor on your own past work, with right answers they have not seen.[^3][^7]
A named person signs off every AI output before it leaves the building.[^14][^16]

headings.what-it-is: What is generative AI consulting, and what does it change?

summary: Generative AI consulting helps you pick a few writing, document and search tasks, choose safe tools and measure the result.[^1][^2] The AI drafts and summarizes; your people check it, because it can state false things confidently.[^3] Redesigning the work, not the model, makes or breaks it.[^4][^5]

answers.walk-away: You should walk away with two or three ranked tasks, a test set, approved tools, trained staff and a plan your team can run alone.
answers.spokes: Most firms of 40 to 500 staff need document help first, then rules and approved tools. Custom builds come last, only after a test shows a gap.
answers.human-role: Your team keeps every sign-off: whoever signs the work checks the AI's draft, like the controller for numbers. AI drafts and searches; people decide.
answers.recipes: The work takes one of three shapes: one writing task for a small team, document-heavy work at a mid-size firm, or fixing shadow AI first.
answers.what-goes-wrong: Most AI pilots stall because they solve the wrong problem, then never reach daily use.[^6][^25]
answers.benchmark: Judge any advisor by a test on your own past work: hidden items with known right answers, scored against today's numbers.[^31][^3]
answers.something-else: Don't hire help when a tool and a rule will do, when you need general business advice, or when staff only need practice.

walkAway: A ranked list of two or three tasks, each with an owner and a metric. Most AI-using firms limit use to three or fewer tasks.[^1][^6]
Today's numbers, plus a test set of past work with known right answers. NIST says to check AI output against known right answers, not impressions.[^3][^7]
Approved business-tier tools and a one-page rule staff can follow. Most AI users bring their own tools to work, and two-thirds of mid-market firms set rules before pilots.[^8][^9]
Trained staff with a review habit. In BCG's survey, five or more hours of training raised regular use from 67% to 79%.[^10][^11]
A plan your team can run without the advisor, with tool accounts and the test set in your firm's name. In RSM's 2025 survey, 62% found generative AI harder to put in place than expected.[^12][^13]

spokes.why: Document analysis is one of the top generative AI tasks at US firms.[^1]
Rules and approved tools, before pilots. Most staff who use AI bring their own tools to work.[^8][^9]
For when your leaders cannot agree on the first task. Picking the wrong problem is the top cause of AI project failure.[^6]
For when one task works and you want a repeatable, multi-step flow. Redesigning the workflow drives most of the profit effect.[^4]
For when the AI must read your finance system (ERP) or customer database (CRM). Legacy integration is a barrier for 28% of mid-market firms.[^9]
Last, only when a test on your own work shows bought tools fall short. In MIT's directional study, partnerships reached use about twice as often as internal builds.[^27]
The overview: when outside help pays, and what it costs to hire an AI team yourself. Most mid-market firms say they need outside help.[^12]

humanRole: A US court fined lawyers $5,000 for filing AI-invented cases, citing their gatekeeping role.[^14][^3]
The customer service lead signs off anything AI says to customers. A Canadian tribunal held an airline responsible for its website chatbot's wrong answer.[^16][^3]
Experts keep the judgement calls AI handles badly. In a study of 758 consultants, AI users were 19 points less likely to be right on such a task.[^17][^3]

AI takes first drafts and search; your people keep the job and add oversight work. In Census data, 66% of AI-using firms only use AI to assist staff on tasks, and 2% report AI-related job decreases.[^1][^5]

recipes.name: 1. Small team, one writing task (about 40 to 100 staff)
recipes.when: Pick this when a team drafts the same kind of document every week. Writing is the leading generative AI task at US firms.[^1][^22]
flow: Ops lead: pick one writing task and record today's time per item and error rate
IT lead: switch on one business-tier tool for a pilot group
Staff: take five or more hours of hands-on training
Team lead: review every output for the first month
Ops lead: compare time and errors with the baseline, counting review time
GM: roll out to other teams or sites only when both numbers improve
recipes.cost: Business seats list at $14 to $25 a user a month (vendor pages, read 26 Nov 2026).[^50][^39] Training adds about $270 a person: five hours at the BLS employer cost of $54.00 an hour.[^19][^10]

recipes.name: 2. Mid-size firm, document-heavy work (about 100 to 500 staff)
recipes.when: Pick this when teams read contracts, claims, reports or files all day. Document analysis and information search lead generative AI use at US firms.[^1]
flow: COO: choose two or three document tasks and name an owner for each
Analyst: build a test set of past documents with known right answers
IT lead: set who may see which files before any tool connects
Controller or reviewer: sign off outputs before anyone acts on them
Division head: decide go or no-go on a date set at the start
recipes.cost: One seat at $25 list costs $300 a year (vendor pages, read 26 Nov 2026).[^40][^39] Even at the all-worker average of 2% of hours saved, one full-time user gives back about $2,246 a year at BLS employer cost.[^20][^19]

recipes.name: 3. Shadow AI first (any size; staff already use unapproved personal AI tools)
recipes.when: Pick this when staff already paste work into personal AI accounts. Most AI users bring their own tools, and personal plans can train on prompts.[^8][^37]
flow: IT lead: survey which AI tools staff use today
Ops lead: move that work to a business-tier plan that does not train on prompts
HR lead: publish a one-page usage rule and run training
Team leads: spot-check outputs every week
recipes.cost: Microsoft's Copilot Business add-on lists at $21 a user a month billed yearly (read 26 Nov 2026).[^47] The UK cyber agency's shadow AI guidance is free.[^29]

ownData.note: Method: each vendor's own pages, read 26 Nov 2026; US list prices before tax and promotions, billed yearly unless stated. Limits: these are vendor statements, not audits, terms change, and quote-only Enterprise tiers are left out. This is not legal advice; firms in regulated sectors need their own review.

watchOuts: Wrong problem: misreading the problem or the metric was the top cause in RAND's study, so agree one measured task first.[^6][^26]
Pilots never reach daily use: S&P Global found firms scrapped 46% of trial projects (proofs of concept) on average. Set a go or no-go date and a production owner before the pilot starts.[^25][^26]

Confident wrong answers: courts have logged over 2,000 decisions on AI-invented content.[^15][^3] A consulting report to a national government drew a partial refund over fake references, so a named reviewer checks every fact.[^28]
Staff leak data through personal tools: in PagerDuty's survey, 34% had put customer data into public AI.[^30][^29] Give them a business-tier plan and a short rule.[^38][^49]
AI used outside what it does well: consultants using AI on such a task were 19 points less likely to be right.[^17] Test each task separately and keep experts on judgement calls.[^18]
Leaders keener than staff: in RSM's survey, 85% say leaders are more enthusiastic than employees.[^9] Only 36% of staff feel trained, so fund five or more hours of hands-on practice.[^10]
howToTest: Record today's numbers for one task: time per item, error rate and rework.[^31]
Pull 50 to 100 past items with known right answers, and keep them hidden from the advisor.[^3][^33]
Write pass and fail criteria before any demo, not after.[^32][^7]
Have the advisor run their approach on your items, in the tool you will actually use.[^31]
Score the output against the right answers, and have your reviewer check a sample. Only 27% of firms in McKinsey's survey review all generative AI output.[^3][^4]
Compare time and errors with today's baseline, counting the time spent reviewing.[^31]
Price the lift: hours saved times employer cost, minus seats. BLS puts a full-time private-sector worker at $54.00 an hour worked (June 2026).[^19]
Ask where not to use AI. It helps on some tasks and hurts on others, so an advisor who says "everything" has not tested.[^17]
Re-test every month, because models and vendor terms change.[^7][^43]

faq.q: What does a generative AI consultant do?
faq.a: A generative AI consultant helps you pick a few writing, document and search tasks, set safe tools and rules, train staff and measure results.[^1][^4] Good ones redesign the work around review, since the AI can be confidently wrong.[^3]

faq.q: How much does it cost to hire an AI consultant?
faq.a: Consulting fees depend on scope, but business-tier AI seats list at $14 to $25 a user a month (read 26 Nov 2026).[^50][^39] Staff time is the other cost: five hours of training is about $270 a person at BLS employer cost.[^19][^10] Small Business Development Centers also give free one-on-one advising.[^34][^35]

faq.q: Is generative AI consulting worth it for a mid-sized firm?
faq.a: Only if you leave with a measured result on your own work.[^6][^3] In RSM's 2025 survey, 70% of mid-market firms said they need outside help.[^12] MIT's directional study found partnerships reached use about twice as often as internal builds.[^27]

faq.q: Will generative AI take my staff's jobs?
faq.a: Not for most firms, on current evidence: 66% of AI-using US firms only use AI to assist staff, and 2% report AI-related job decreases.[^1] In a study of 5,172 support agents, the least experienced gained most, resolving 30% more issues an hour.[^18]

faq.q: Is it safe to let staff use ChatGPT with company data?
faq.a: Only on a business-tier plan, not a personal one. Personal ChatGPT may train on chats unless the user opts out; ChatGPT Business does not by default.[^37][^38] Our table above compares four vendors.

faq.q: Should we build a custom AI tool or use what we already have?
faq.a: Use what you already have first, and build only when a test on your own work shows a gap.[^27][^3] Our custom AI solutions guide covers when building pays.

pickElse: Your team just needs a tool and a rule. Buy ChatGPT Business, Claude Team, Microsoft 365 Copilot Business or Gemini in Google Workspace, and use the vendor's admin setup.[^39][^44]
You need general business advice, not AI work: a local Small Business Development Center gives free one-on-one advising.[^34][^35]
Your staff need skills, not a project: run five or more hours of hands-on practice in the tool you already pay for. BCG's survey ties that much training to more regular use.[^10]
The task is high stakes and outside what AI does well: keep it with your experts.[^17][^14]

offer.heading: Find the first task AI should help with
offer.body: Free, before any paid work: 30 minutes on one writing, document or research task your team does every week. Leave with today's number to beat, the business-tier plan that fits your data rules and a fair test.

reviews.notes: Dana got what to ask for, who does what in each build and how to test the advisor. Tripped on 'business plan': it read as a business-plan document, not an AI subscription tier. Now 'business-tier plan' everywhere. Asked how long the work takes; the research has no neutral time source, so the page gives the one-month review window and a go or no-go date, with no project length.

Tripped on 'augment tasks', 'proofs of concept', 'foundation models', 'shadow AI' and 'Entra ID'. Each is now plain: AI assists staff rather than taking over tasks, trial projects (proofs of concept), the underlying AI models, unapproved personal AI tools, Microsoft Entra ID work accounts. ERP and CRM were already spelled out.

Asked whether one team or site can pilot first and what it does to the unit's numbers. The small-team build now ends with the GM rolling out only when time and errors both improve. The price-the-lift test step turns hours into dollars at the BLS employer cost; no unit-margin figure exists in the research.

Read as the COO hiring the help, the division head for this page. Wanted the handover to be real: the walk-away bullet now asks for tool accounts and the test set in the firm's name. Each build already names the role at every step, and the test steps keep the right answers hidden from the advisor.

Steve got the answer from the title and bottom line in 10 seconds: a few measured tasks, a business-tier tool, people stay in charge. Wanted payback per person: the mid-size build now sets one $300-a-year seat against about $2,246 a year of time back at the all-worker average, labelled as an average. Data safety is covered by the own-data table. No Zavient price is shown, per the lead's rule.
